title: Azure AI Foundry Pricing: Cost Breakdown (2026 Guide)
summary: Azure AI Foundry pricing charges per model with no platform fee. One team's $210 surprise alert shows why budget limits are essential before costs spike.
body_markdown:
## Azure AI Foundry monthly cost example


At 360 million tokens a month, the ticket classifier and summariser costs $2,400 on Standard, $1,200 on Batch and $3,900 on Reserved PTU. Those figures come from[a 2026 Azure OpenAI pricing breakdown](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/azure-openai-pricing-2026-is-ptu-worth-the-cost) .


Pick the wrong tier and **the monthly cost moves by up to $2,700** . The same work can cost more than three times as much depending on how you buy it.


### Budget versus invoice, line by line


Only the first two lines show up in the headline price. The table below sets each against what a team usually budgets, and the other five arrive on the invoice anyway, so the budget column is where the surprise starts.


Bill line Budgeted Invoiced Same month with Batch, caching and reservation


Input tokens Counted Billed per million Batch halves the rate; caching cuts repeated prompt text


Output tokens Counted Billed per million Batch halves the rate


Retries Not counted Billed as fresh tokens Still billed; fewer failures at steady capacity


AI Search Not counted Billed as its own meter Unchanged by any of the three


Content safety Not counted Billed per call Unchanged


Logging Not counted Billed by data stored Unchanged


Egress Not counted Billed by data leaving Azure Unchanged


You can't discount away the five side meters, because Batch and caching only touch the token lines. Budget for them separately, or they become the overrun.


### Azure AI Foundry cost with Batch and caching


Choose Standard instead of Batch and the monthly expense doubles, since Batch cuts the $2,400 Standard month to $1,200. That's half, in exchange for waiting on results instead of getting them instantly.


Some work can wait and some can't: overnight ticket summaries can, a live agent-assist reply can't. Split the work by that test and only pay Standard rates for what truly needs speed.


### Azure AI Foundry reservation break-even point


At $3,900 a month, Reserved PTU, a block of capacity you pay for whether or not you use it, costs $1,500 more than Standard at 360 million tokens, and $2,700 more than Batch.


Doing nothing about this is the expensive option: reserving at this volume means paying for idle capacity.


By simple arithmetic, Standard scales with usage at roughly $6.67 per million tokens. A $3,900 reservation therefore only breaks even near 585 million tokens a month, and only if the reserved capacity can actually absorb that load.


Decide that threshold before the first invoice, not after it.


Only if something watches it does a cap help. Activepieces, an open-source tool for chaining automated steps together, can do that watching on a schedule and alert a person, or ask for their approval, when spend crosses your line.


The LICENSE file in its GitHub repository shows an MIT-licensed core, the pricing page lists unlimited flows on the free plan, and a run costs 1 credit however many steps it has, so a check on a timer draws on the free plan's 1,000 monthly credits one run at a time.


Open the run detail view for any run and each step is listed separately with its own input and output, so the spend figure the check read and the branch it took are on record, and the enterprise RBAC docs show access policies applying to what a workflow may connect to.
